In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
DMFT is not yet ready to be employed as a tool to study QTAIM and IQAs.
DMFT provides a reasonable approximation to the 2 RDM and that QTAIM and IQAs can be used to extract chemically relevant information from these approximate 2 R DMs.
DMFT is a promising approach to the QTAIM, with a number of limitations and caveats that need to be taken into account.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the DMFTs are very promising in the context of the QTAIM and that the IQA approach is an excellent tool to assess the quality of DMFTs.

DMFTs perform well for the QTAIM and IQAs, with the notable exception of the exchange correlation energies, where the performance is strongly dependent on the functional used, the level of theory, and the molecule studied.

, in general, DMFT performs quite well, especially in the case of the natural orbital functionals, which are the most accurate ones, but that it is still far from providing a reliable description of the chemical bonding and of the energy partitioning in molecules.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, while the DMFT is not able to provide accurate total energies, its performance in terms of the QTAIM descriptors is quite good, especially for the more sophisticated functionals.
the DMFT is an excellent approximation to the exact 2-RDM for most molecules and reactions studied here.

the QTAIM and IQAs are able to provide a physically sound partitioning of the total energy and the exchange correlation energy in a molecule, and that the DMFT is a viable tool to obtain such quantities in a computationally efficient way.
